items.t: China Spurs Biggest Stock Gain Since 2024 on Rare Midday Vow
sum: Chinese authorities gave markets a boost with a rare midday statement pledging support, sending stocks to their best day in more than two years.

The State Council pledged to boost the role of the so-called national team and improve policies guiding long-term funds into stocks, according to the Xinhua News Agency. The authorities said they would also crack down on financial fraud while encouraging listed companies to step up dividend payouts and share buybacks.

The securities regulator later vowed in a statement to cooperate with other authorities to speed up the study and adoption of policies to stabilize capital markets. The commission’s chairman, Wu Qing, hosted a meeting to go over the outcomes of the earlier State Council gathering.

The CSI 300 Index, an onshore benchmark, jumped 4.2%, the biggest one-day gain since October 2024. Tech stocks were among the biggest gainers, with the chip-heavy Star 50 Index surging 15% in its third-best day ever. The optimism spread to Hong Kong, where the Hang Seng Tech Index advanced 6.5%.

Chances of a macro policy pivot by Chinese authorities have risen with such a rare move, according to Citigroup Inc. Friday’s State Council meeting “reaffirmed the policy put for capital markets, and raised the sense of urgency to a new high, ” said economists led by Xiangrong Yu. Explicit discussion of “national team” and “quasi-stabilization fund” in the readout also confirmed such urgency, they added.

Even with few fresh measures, the statement boosted sentiment with its timing and authoritative heft in addressing the role of the national team. Most Chinese stock benchmarks had tumbled into a bear market this year as tepid earnings and a weak economy gave investors little reason to buy following a global tech rout. However, investors took heart in the rare policy signal in the readout, with total stock market turnover climbing to 2 trillion yuan , the most in nearly a month.

“The intent is unequivocal: policymakers want to stabilize market sentiment,” said Chen Shi, a fund manager at Shanghai Jade Stone Investment Management Co. “This is now the second State Council meeting this month to underscore the importance of capital-market stability.”

Bombay HC quashes ICICI board approval to prosecute Chanda Kochhar
sum: Justice Milind Jadhav, in an order, said ICICI Bank's board of directors is not the competent authority to grant sanction for prosecution under Section 19 of the PC (Prevention of Corruption) Act; instead, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) ought to have granted such sanction.

"The special court ought not to mechanically have taken cognisance of the chargesheet in petitioner's (Kochhar's) case and instead ought to have carefully perused the impugned sanction to understand whether the authority that granted it was competent to do so in law in the present case," said the court in its 57-page order.

The court also declined the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)'s request to stay the order for eight weeks to challenge its legality and validity.

Kamarajar Port picks SBI Capital, IDBI Capital and ICICI Securities for IPO
sum: Chennai-based Kamarajar Port Ltd has picked three investment banks for an initial public offering (IPO) that would make it India's first listed state-backed port.

The country's first corporate major port has hired SBI Capital Markets Ltd, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities Ltd, and ICICI Securities Ltd as the book-running lead managers for the offer, two people aware of the development told Mint.
The IPO is likely to include an offer for sale of about ₹1,200 crore, while a fresh issue could be decided at a later stage, a document issued by the port earlier in September showed.
Emails sent to Kamarajar Port, SBI Capital, IDBI Capital and ICICI Securities on 14 November did not elicit responses until press time.

Mint had reported on 13 September that the Chennai Port Authority, which wholly owns Kamarajar Port, had begun the process of seeking up to three bookrunning lead managers to structure and manage the issue.

India's public markets currently have three listed port entities: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd (APSEZ), JSW Infrastructure Ltd and APM Terminals-backed Gujarat Pipavav Port Ltd. A successful IPO would make Kamarajar the only listed state-backed port in the country.

Established in 1999, Kamarajar is one of India’s 12 major ports and the country’s first corporate major port, functioning under the ministry of ports, shipping and waterways. Located in Chennai, it was originally developed as Ennore Port and later renamed after former Tamil Nadu chief minister Kumaraswami Kamaraj.

sum: Quality Assessment: Robust Fundamentals Support Long-Term Strength

ICICI Bank maintains a solid quality profile, underpinned by its strong capital adequacy and asset quality metrics. The bank’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) stands at a healthy 16.07%, comfortably above regulatory requirements, signalling ample buffers against credit risks. Gross Non-Performing Assets (NPA) remain low at 1.20%, reflecting prudent risk management and effective recovery mechanisms.

Return on Assets (ROA) is steady at 2.01%, with the latest quarterly figures showing an average ROA of 2.13%, indicating efficient utilisation of assets to generate profits. The bank’s net profit has grown at an annualised rate of 23.44%, demonstrating consistent earnings growth. Additionally, the bank declared a Dividend Per Share (DPS) of ₹12.00 for the year, the highest in recent periods, highlighting management’s confidence in cash flow stability.

Institutional investors hold a significant 92.44% stake in ICICI Bank, reflecting strong confidence from sophisticated market participants who typically conduct rigorous fundamental analysis. With a market capitalisation of ₹9,92,261 crores, ICICI Bank is the second largest entity in the private banking sector, accounting for 28.43% of the sector’s market cap. Its annual sales of ₹1,80,022 crores represent 18.31% of the industry, underscoring its dominant market position.
Valuation: Shift from Attractive to Expensive Raises Caution

The valuation grade for ICICI Bank has been downgraded from attractive to expensive, primarily due to its elevated price multiples relative to peers and historical averages. The bank’s Price-to-Earnings (PE) ratio currently stands at 16.80, which is higher than HDFC Bank’s 13.7 and Axis Bank’s 12.86, though lower than Kotak Mahindra Bank’s 21.69. The Price-to-Book (P/B) ratio is 2.77, signalling a premium valuation compared to the sector average.

The Price/Earnings to Growth (PEG) ratio is 1.86, indicating that the stock’s price growth is outpacing earnings growth, which may limit upside potential. Dividend yield remains modest at 0.87%, which, while stable, does not offer significant income support for investors.

ICICI Life Stock: Is Wider Valuation Discount a Buying Opportunity?
sum: When the worth of a business rises but its share price falls, investors have a reason to take a closer look. ICICI Life Insurance (formerly ICICI Prudential Life Insurance) presents just such an opportunity.

In December 2025, the private-sector life insurer stock was attractively valued at ₹651, or about 1.9 times its embedded value. This was at a good discount to like-sized peers. Since then, the stock has corrected sharply. At around ₹456 on November 13, 2026, it was down 30 per cent from its December 19 close. In comparison, SBI Life Insurance, Max Financial Services (holding company for Axis Max Life Insurance) and HDFC Life Insurance have fallen in 12-23 per cent. Concerns over uneven sales growth, proposed regulatory changes and Prudential’s planned stake reduction have weighed on sentiment.

Yet, ICICI Life’s underlying business has moved in the opposite direction. Embedded value, which captures shareholders’ net worth and expected future profits from existing policies, grew 12.2 per cent year-on-year by September 2026. New business profitability has improved too.

Trading at nearly 1.2 times embedded value, the ICICI Life Insurance stock now offers considerably better valuation comfort. Hence, existing investors can consider increasing their exposure while new investors can also consider adding it to their portfolio with a long-term perspective.

ICICI Life sells term insurance for family protection, traditional savings and guaranteed-income plans, and ULIPs that combine life cover with stock market-linked investments. It also offers pension and annuity plans for retirement income, besides group insurance covering employees and borrowers, including those taking home loans.
One notable development is that ICICI Life is not just selling more insurance. It also expects higher profits from the new policies it sells.

In the first half of FY27, annualised premium equivalent (APE), a standard measure of new insurance sales, grew 15.1 per cent to ₹4,935 crore. This compares with a 4.1 per cent decline in the corresponding period last year.

Massive surge! Reliance Industries shares up 12% after Q2; add ₹2 lakh cr in mcap — when did RIL last rally this much?
sum: The shares finished Monday’s trade with a solid 12% jump to settle at ₹1,300 on NSE, their highest level since early September. The stock last posted a comparable single-day surge in April 2020. Given its heavyweight status in the Nifty 50, the rally also lifted the index by 1.7%, even as tensions in West Asia remained elevated.

For long-term Reliance Industries shareholders, the sharp rise has revived confidence in the stock, which had been trending lower since the start of 2026. The shares closed in the red in eight of the previous 10 months. Despite Monday’s rebound, the stock remains down 17.22% so far this year.

The double-digit jump in the stock added ₹1.84 lakh crore to the company’s market capitalisation, taking it to ₹17.6 lakh crore and helping it retain its position as India’s most valuable listed company.

At its peak of ₹1,611, the company commanded a market capitalisation of ₹21.8 lakh crore. It had crossed the ₹21 lakh crore mark in June 2024, becoming the first Indian company to achieve this milestone.

Meanwhile, investors in the Reliance Group have another reason to celebrate, as its telecom arm, Jio Platforms, made a blockbuster stock market debut last week, listing at ₹1,440 apiece, a premium of 21.3% over its issue price.

Reliance Industries Ltd reported a record consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹29,550 crore for the July-September quarter (Q2 FY27), marking a 33.8% increase from ₹22,092 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue rose 27.8% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record ₹62,409 crore.

The strong performance was primarily driven by a recovery in the oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business, where EBITDA surged 67.9% to ₹25,203 crore, supported by higher global fuel margins and improved petrochemical spreads. O2C revenue increased 44.2% to ₹2,31,601 crore, with supply disruptions in West Asia and other regions pushing transportation fuel cracks higher.

sum: The listing of Jio Platforms has put the spotlight on India’s telecom sector, with investors now weighing whether the newly listed Reliance Industries-backed company or established rival Bharti Airtel offers a better investment opportunity.

Jio Platforms shares have surged nearly 28% from their issue price of ₹1,119 since making their market debut on Wednesday, 28 October, taking its market capitalisation to nearly ₹13.18 lakh crore and making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after Reliance Industries. The strong debut and subsequent gains follow an IPO that attracted bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, has built a strong long-term track record, with its shares delivering returns of 586.10% over the past decade and 187.07% over five years. However, the stock remains down 6.64% so far in 2026. With Jio commanding a substantial valuation and Airtel offering an established earnings track record, which telecom stock should investors consider now? Experts weigh in on their growth prospects, valuations and investment appeal.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, remains a stronger proposition for investors seeking earnings visibility, higher ARPU, robust cash flows and disciplined capital allocation. Experts say investors should weigh valuations, earnings growth and execution risks before choosing between the two telecom stocks.

Gaurav Arora, Head of Research at SAHI, said Jio’s listing at a valuation of around ₹10.3 lakh crore places it among India’s top five companies by market capitalisation from day one. This, he said, changes the investment question from assessing the company’s growth potential to evaluating the returns investors can realistically expect from current levels. Companies of this scale rarely grow significantly faster than the broader economy, making low double-digit annual returns a reasonable base case.

He also noted that ARPU growth in India has historically been uneven, with increases largely coming through tariff hikes in 2019, 2021 and 2024. These hikes have typically required coordinated moves by all three telecom operators and have depended on regulatory considerations, making it difficult to factor in consistent ARPU growth over a 10-year investment horizon.

items.t: Kotak Mahindra Bank stock reaches record high as outlook brightens
sum: Kotak Mahindra Bank shares reached a record high on Thursday, October 29, as improving growth prospects and expectations for stronger earnings lifted investor sentiment. The Economic Times reported that the shares closed at INR 457 on the BSE, up 3.86 percent from the previous close, after touching INR 460 intraday.

The report said analysts expect earnings to improve as credit growth accelerates, funds raised through foreign-currency non-resident deposits are deployed and higher lending rates pass through. Better asset quality, lower credit costs and improved cost ratios are also expected to support profitability.

Axis Securities expects Kotak Mahindra Bank to deliver a return on assets of 2.1 to 2.2 percent and a return on equity of 12 to 14 percent over fiscal 2027 to fiscal 2029. The brokerage said those measures would place the bank second among large private-sector lenders, behind ICICI Bank.

Kotak Mahindra Bank's investor-relations page reports consolidated second-quarter profit after tax of INR 5,645 crore and customer assets of INR 699,250 crore. Standalone deposits reached INR 651,491 crore, while the net interest margin stood at 4.31 percent.

The bank also reported a 22.4 percent capital adequacy ratio, a 22.1 percent common-equity tier-one ratio and annualised returns on assets and equity of 2.10 percent and 11.70 percent, respectively. These figures give investors a reference point for assessing whether the expected recovery in growth can translate into more durable profitability.

Kotak Mahindra Bank is an Indian financial-services group with banking, lending, deposits and related customer-asset businesses. Its operations serve retail, corporate and other banking customers through a nationwide branch network and digital platforms. The available company material identifies the bank as a diversified Indian private-sector lender, but does not establish a directly comparable competitor set for this report.

sum: The stock had climbed to Rs 93.60 on Wednesday, its highest level in nearly two weeks, taking IDBI Bank’s market capitalisation above Rs 1 lakh crore. The rally followed the Cabinet’s approval of the sale of the government’s and LIC’s combined stake to Fairfax Financial Holdings’ subsidiary, M/s 10955230 Canada Inc., for Rs 52,878.08 crore.

The deal marks a major step in the lender’s transformation after years of financial stress. Fairfax’s bid of Rs 81 per share was above the Rs 75.99 average fair valuation arrived at by two independent professional valuation agencies.

The government will retain a 15% stake in IDBI Bank, while LIC will hold 19% after the transaction. The successful bidder will also have to go through the RBI’s ‘fit & proper’ assessment and secure other regulatory approvals before the deal is completed.

IDBI Bank today looks very different from the lender that once needed repeated government support. Its gross NPA ratio has fallen from 31.78% in September 2018 to 2.32% in March 2026, while net NPAs have dropped from 17.30% to 0.15%.

The improvement has also shown up in profitability and growth. IDBI Bank reported a net profit of Rs 9,513 crore in FY26, while its total business rose 18% year-on-year to Rs 6.27 lakh crore as of September 30. Its latest quarterly business update showed deposits rising 17% to Rs 3.56 lakh crore and net advances growing 18% to Rs 2.72 lakh crore.

Bank of Baroda shares drop 3% after NMC Healthcare founder BR Shetty files $15 bn lawsuit; lender issues c
sum: Bank of Baroda shares tumbled to Rs 230.40 apiece on NSE. This came after BR Shetty’s reported lawsuit, filed at the Bombay High Court, sought $5 billion in direct damages for alleged fraud and negligence, $5 billion in consequential damages and $5 billion in compensation for reputational harm arising from various actions taken by the bank, including a lookout circular issued against him. He also sought 18% interest on the first $10 billion, the ET report added.
Also read | Bank of Baroda to pay $600 million to settle NMC Health insolvency claims

Shetty’s lawsuit names Bank of Baroda, many of its current and former executives, former NMC employees, along with other individuals and companies, ET reported. His case is linked to one in the UAE that Bank of Baroda settled in July by paying roughly $600 million (around Rs 5,700 crore) to the administrators of the insolvent NMC and its affiliates. Administrators of the UAE-based healthcare group had accused Bank of Baroda of facilitating improper transactions in cahoots with Shetty, without doing due diligence and following proper anti-money-laundering and customer verification processes.

UAE-based healthcare provider NMC Health was declared insolvent in 2020 after it was found that it had hidden more than $4 billion in debt. Besides BoB, other creditors to the company are Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank, Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank, Dubai Islamic Bank, Emirates NBD among others.
Following the sharp drop in share price, Bank of Baroda issued a clarification to exchanges, stating that it has not been served with such a suit.

Bank of Baroda shares have fallen more than 1% in a week and nearly 3% in a month, with the stock overall being down 23% in 2026 so far, underperforming the Nifty Next 50 index which is down only 1% during the same time.

The shares of the PSU lender have dropped over 12% in one year. In the longer term, the stock delivered positive returns of nearly 14% in three years and 161% in five years. The company’s market capitalisation stands at around Rs 1.2 lakh crore.

Stock market holiday: Is Indian stock market open or closed on 19th March for Gudi Padwa 2026?
sum: Gudi Padwa will be celebrated on Thursday, 19 March 2026, across Maharashtra. The festival marks the Marathi New Year and signifies the arrival of spring, the conclusion of the Rabi harvest season, and the beginning of a new year filled with hope, prosperity, and renewal. However, Indian stock market investors will watch out whether it is a trading holiday tomorrow as both the major stock exchanges - BSE and the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) - are based in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

The BSE stock market holiday calendar shows no trading holiday tomorrow on March 19. The trading holiday list for 2026 does not include March 19 as a stock market holiday. Hence, there is no stock market holiday on Gudi Padwa 2026.
The trading on both the stock exchanges, BSE and NSE, will continue as per the normal trading timing on Gudi Padwa, March 19.
However, trading Currency Derivatives Segments & NDS-RST and Tri Party Repo segments will remain closed tomorrow, as Gudi Padwa will be a bank holiday.

The list of stock market holidays 2026 shows that the trading in the Equity Segment and Equity Derivative Segment will remain open on March 19, while Currency Derivatives Segments & NDS-RST and Tri-Party Repo segments will be closed tomorrow.
Additionally, trading in Commodity Derivatives and Electronic Gold Receipts (EGR) segments will also remain open tomorrow.
The previous stock market trading holiday fell on 3 March 2026, Tuesday, on account of Holi. The BSE and NSE were closed and no trading took place on that day.

Why Banking and Insurance Stocks Are Falling Today - March 06, 2026
sum: Shares of several banking and life insurance companies came under pressure today after the Reserve Bank of India proposed tighter rules on how insurance products are sold along with bank loans.
The move targets a common practice in the financial sector bundling insurance policies with loans, particularly credit protection insurance.
While the proposal is aimed at improving transparency for customers, investors are worried that it could slow down a profitable segment of the insurance business and reduce fee income for banks.
Here is a simple breakdown of what is happening and why the market reacted negatively.

Banks often sell insurance products alongside loans such as home loans, personal loans, or car loans. This model is known as bancassurance, where banks act as distribution partners for insurance companies.
Under the proposed rules, banks will no longer be able to automatically attach insurance policies to loans. Customers will have to explicitly agree to buy the insurance product.
